gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate NAS costs to run around the clock. From the makers' own wattage figures at the August 2026 US average of 18.16¢/kWh, that is $26/yr for the UGREEN DXP2800, $27 for the Synology DS225+, $32 for the DS725+, $36 for the Asustor AS5402T, $46 for the QNAP TS-264, $60 for the DS925+ and $67 for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus with drives active, and $8 to $29/yr with drives spun down.
standout_why: I compared against rackdiff.com 'Paperless-ngx Hosting: NAS vs VPS Comparison 2026'. It tells readers to 'work out your device's consumption with your electricity rate' and leaves the power line of its 3-year cost table empty. It gives no wattage for any model. peira.dev's Paperless NAS playbook names no NAS model and gives no power figure. The cited docs.paperless-ngx.com setup page returned 403 to me. ChatGPT read it as saying a Raspberry Pi is enough, and none of ChatGPT's four answers mentions power draw or running cost. No rival result gives a yearly running cost for any model.
decides: This confirms the 2-bay picks for a mostly idle document archive. The DXP2800 ($389.99 at UGREEN today) is the cheapest to buy among the UGREEN picks and the cheapest to run of all the candidates: $26.06/yr against $46.27 for the TS-264. That gap is about $101 over 5 years. It also weakens the 4-bay 'headroom' picks ChatGPT pushed. By each maker's figure with drives active, the DXP4800 Plus ($67.39/yr) and DS925+ ($60.31/yr) cost roughly 2.3 to 2.6 times as much to run as the DXP2800, and Paperless alone does not need them. Warning: the makers test differently (UGREEN uses one 2 TB drive, QNAP fills every bay, Asustor doesn't say). So the cross-brand gaps are rough, but each model's own figure holds.
